- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% for the following 3–5 periods.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% higher), check sentiment for recent bullishness — if present, consider mean reversion bias and reduce forecast by 1–3% per day.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% lower), sentiment is often bearish — consider a small upward adjustment (1–3%) to avoid missing reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early mean reversion; if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral/bearish, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
